candidates.rationale: When the best day of the last fortnight dwarfs the worst, the stock has been bid up by lottery-seeking and attention flow rather than information, and that premium unwinds once the flow stops.

A profitable firm whose drift arrives smoothly (small daily steps, one direction) is being accumulated on information and keeps drifting, while the same net move delivered in jagged spikes is liquidity noise that reverts.
An open above yesterday's high is an overnight order-imbalance shock, and in firms with a large accrual gap (weak earnings quality) it is least likely to be real news, so the gap gets filled.

Negative daily return autocorrelation is bid-ask bounce, so it proxies the effective spread: harder-to-trade names earn an illiquidity premium and their prints overshoot fair value in both directions.

Close-to-close volatility that exceeds what the intraday range can explain arrived overnight as news jumps, and jump information is absorbed slowly, so a high overnight share of variance predicts continued drift.
A single-session range blow-out in a stable, highly profitable firm is liquidity demand rather than fundamental news, so the concession paid to absorb it is refunded within days.

The share of the last three weeks' total trading range that sits above the opening prints measures persistent intraday buying pressure, and institutions work large orders over many sessions, so unfinished demand keeps pushing.
A stock whose range expands on down days and contracts on up days has fear-driven holders and asymmetric downside risk, which is compensated with higher expected returns.

Operating efficiency improved over the last quarter while the price just fell means the market has not yet paid for the fundamental news, so post-earnings drift and one-week reversal push the same way.

In profitable firms a one-week drop is liquidity-driven and gets bought back, while in unprofitable ones the same drop is news about deterioration that continues, so centering profitability flips reversal into momentum exactly where each belongs.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Shift proposal budget toward mixed niches: they returned 3.14-5.04 this round versus 0.03-2.84 for pure price_volume, across all three speeds.
  2. Swapping only the outer wrapper (CS_RANK to CS_DEMEAN or CS_ZSCORE) or replacing one leaf with its TS_MEAN over a new window is not novelty; all five archive_subtree rejections were exactly that, sharing 5-12 nodes. Change the operator skeleton or the data fields instead.
  3. Three mutations landed 4-8 edits away because a fresh short expression was attached to an unrelated parent. Either pick a parent that already shares the skeleton and change one window or one field, or submit the idea as a new seed rather than a mutation.
  4. Track proposals already made this run before submitting bare single-fundamental ranks: both duplicates were canonical one-liners over $roa and $roe.
  5. Stop normalising by a guarded mean of a raw field. TS_MEAN($volume,21)+1e-8, TS_MEAN($high,21)+1e-8 and TS_MEAN($high,126)+1e-8 each drew an archive_subtree hit (5 shared nodes, 3 rejects). Every accept normalised by a derived series instead: TS_MEAN($high-$low,63), TS_SUM($high-$low,10), TS_SUM(ABS($return),21), TS_STD($return,w).
  6. The TS_CORR($high-$low, dollar-volume, 63) family is exhausted. Raw $dollar_volume, /$open and /TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,63) all returned rho 0.961 to 0.977 against the same archive member. The two that cleared put the volume leg through TS_DELTA(...,5) or TS_RANK(...,10) and shortened the correlation window to 21, so change the leg's transform and the window together, not the normaliser.
  7. Return legs only clear the cheap screen as self-normalising ratios. Short-over-long TS_STD (5 over 63) and TS_MAX/TS_SUM of ABS($return) at 21 sat at fitness 2.25 to 4.11; single-window TS_STD at 63 and 105, and TS_DECAY_LINEAR over TS_STD, stalled at |t| 0.89 to 0.97.
  8. Drop raw $close kernels. $close/DELAY($close,w) ratios were the weakest cheap-screen bucket by a wide margin (|t| 0.42, 0.45, 0.50), and CS_RANK(TS_RANK($close,10)) is an alpha101 subtree.
  9. Directional return aggregates buy almost nothing. SIGN sums, TS_MEAN/TS_STD sharpe forms, TS_ARGMAX(ABS($return),63) and summed raw OHLC gaps produced the three weakest accepts (0.382, 0.591, 0.603). Dispersion, concentration and correlation kernels produced everything above 1.9.
  10. CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) as a leading term is spent: in one round it drew both a 5-node archive_subtree hit and a rho 0.901 correlation hit against the same archive member. CS_ZSCORE or plain CS_RANK on $accrual_gap and $asset_turnover carried the 3.1 to 4.1 accepts.
  11. Rescaling a window is not a decorrelating edit. The 126-day channel-position kernel came back rho 0.858 against its 21-day twin. Spend mutation edits on replacing a whole leg; the one non-local reject wasted its budget scattering edits across wrapper, leg and window at once.
  12. Keep total lookback at 126 days or less. A DELAY($close,189) leg was the round's only coverage failure at 0.896; every expression at 126 or below cleared the gate, including 126-day TS_CORR.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
